no_junk_drawer_directories.instructions: Does the project structure avoid flat junk-drawer directories that dump many loosely related files or multiple distinct concerns into one folder?

criteria.pass: Directories stay focused and navigable—each folder holds a cohesive set of closely related files or well-organized subfolders rather than a sprawling flat list of unrelated responsibilities.
criteria.fail: One or more directories flatten a large collection of loosely related files or multiple distinct concerns/sub-features into a single crowded folder instead of grouping them into navigable subfolders.

cohesive_subfeature_grouping.instructions: Are tightly related file clusters (sharing a domain prefix or importing mostly from each other) grouped into dedicated subfolders instead of sitting flat alongside unrelated peers?

criteria.pass: Multi-file sub-features, widget families, or tightly coupled helper clusters live together in dedicated subfolders (or stay flat only when the entire parent folder is already small and single-purpose).
criteria.fail: A clear multi-file cluster (such as several files sharing a sub-feature prefix or forming a tight local-import subgraph) is dumped flat into a larger directory alongside unrelated sibling files.

clear_concern_separation.instructions: Are distinct architectural concerns (such as persistence, external API/AI transport, domain models/rules, UI components, orchestration, and test utilities) cleanly separated rather than mixed flat together?

criteria.pass: Distinct layers or concerns (such as storage/persistence, external clients/inference, core domain logic, UI components, and test utilities) are clearly separated by directory or naming boundary, without test-only helpers masquerading as production files.
criteria.fail: Multiple distinct architectural concerns (such as persistence, external transport/API clients, domain logic, and orchestration) are mixed flat in the same directory without clear boundaries, OR un-suffixed test utility files sit alongside production source files.

consistent_organization_depth.instructions: Do sibling sub-features use a consistent level of folder organization rather than partially extracting one sub-feature while leaving comparable peer clusters flat?

criteria.pass: Comparable sub-features or clusters within a directory follow a consistent grouping convention (either peers are similarly grouped into subfolders or the directory is small enough that flat layout is uniform).
criteria.fail: A directory extracts one sub-feature into a dedicated subfolder while leaving equally large or larger multi-file peer clusters flat in the parent directory.

descriptive_file_roles.instructions: Do file and folder names clearly convey ownership without vague catch-all names or confusingly ambiguous generic filenames?

criteria.pass: Files and folders have specific, domain-meaningful names that make ownership obvious, without grab-bag files (such as utils, helpers, common, misc) or ambiguous generic names repeated across related folders.
criteria.fail: The structure relies on vague catch-all filenames (such as utils, helpers, common, misc, or un-scoped test-support), or repeats ambiguous generic names (such as model, service, decisions, languages, validation) across sibling or parent/child folders in ways that obscure what belongs where.
